As a single person who makes good money it pretty much isn’t worth it to cook unless you enjoy it. But if you’re single and barely surviving you don’t really have a choice to cook most meals since saving even a couple hundred every month is the difference between going negative each month in your budget.

But the big thing is when you have a full family to feed, cooking and prepping large meals at home becomes more financially significant. It costs like $100 to feed 5 people at chipotle, while you can whip up something basic and quick at home for 5 people for like $20. Repeat this 30 times a month (and this is just dinner) now you’re at $80x30=$2,400.00 savings. But if you’re only one person this savings is reduced to a couple hundred/month. Also when you buy food at grocery stores it’s way harder to eat it before it goes bad if you’re a single person, so you become more efficient when feeding a family.
